game: ATL@CAR Week 3 2025, kickoff 2025-09-21 13:00 ET, CAR +5.5, total 44.5, outdoors

script.base: Atlanta is a 5.5-point road favorite with a 25.0 implied total against Carolina's 19.5 in a moderate 44.5 outdoor game, not a shootout and not a 10-point blowout. Base flow: ATL leads by about a score from the second half, pace stays average, and the Falcons lean on Bijan Robinson (34 carries, 167 rush yards in two games) with Tyler Allgeier (26/100) to close; Carolina trails and throws, with Bryce Young feeding Tetairoa McMillan (19 targets, 168 yards, 186 air). Starters should play most of the snaps at this spread.
script.flip1: Carolina hangs around or leads at home in a divisional game. ATL cannot clock-kill, so Bijan and Allgeier carry counts stall toward Bijan's 24-yard rushing game, both quarterbacks throw, and Drake London, Kyle Pitts, McMillan and Ja'Tavion Sanders stay live while Chuba Hubbard's carry pace (26 carries, 95 yards) survives.
script.flip2: ATL jumps ahead early and the margin gets to garbage time. Falcons passing stalls after halftime (London 19 targets, Pitts 13) while Allgeier vultures clock carries and Bijan's receiving spike (100 and 25) does not repeat; Carolina abandons Hubbard's rush and Young dumps short, which can still leave empty yards for McMillan, Hunter Renfrow or Sanders if the prevent shell is soft.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse injury report only; final inactives about 90 minutes before kick are not in the pack. ATL WR Casey Washington Out (concussion) removes 6 targets, 33 yards and 99 air yards; that thin deep share nudges Drake London (19 tgt), Ray-Ray McCloud (7 tgt/51 yds) and Darnell Mooney (4 tgt), not a new WR1. ATL WR Jamal Agnew Out (groin) is not in the target log, so no skill-volume gain. ATL CB A.J. Terrell Out (hamstring) is the defensive loss: Carolina WR1 McMillan faces an unnamed backup, and ATL CB Mike Ford is only Questionable (groin), so the secondary is thin. CAR DT Tershawn Wharton Out (hamstring) and CAR LB Patrick Jones II Out (hamstring) weaken the front Atlanta runs into; Jones profiles as an edge, so this is pressure and edge-fit more than a proven TE-coverage hole. CAR WR Xavier Legette Questionable (hamstring) had 15 targets but only 8 yards; if he sits, targets tilt to McMillan, Renfrow (15 tgt), Sanders (12) and Hubbard (11), but he is not ruled out, so no confirmed sleeper. No ATL or CAR skill player on this card is listed out.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC, man/zone or coverage charting in the pack. Location proxy only: CAR YPA left 5.79 (19 att), middle 11.83 (18), right 4.17 (18). ATL YPA left 3.21 (14), middle 12.7 (10), right 5.28 (29).
matchup.pressure: CAR blitz rate 25%; ATL EPA/dropback +0.23 vs blitz vs +0.05 vs none, so Penix is not a pressure problem and Wharton plus Jones being out should dull Carolina's rush further. ATL blitz rate 30%; CAR EPA/dropback -0.35 vs blitz vs -0.04 vs none, so Young is the pressure victim. Pressure that gets home cuts deep WR yards and lifts RB/TE checkdowns.
matchup.bleeds: CAR run defense allows 5.61 YPC and 7 runs of 10+, with only 4 passes of 20+ for 56 yards: they bleed the run and the middle, and are sound to the right (4.17 YPA). ATL allows 4.39 YPC and 4 runs of 10+, plus 4 passes of 20+ for 60 yards: tighter vs the run, bleed is the middle (12.7 YPA on just 10 throws), not a proven deep-right leak.
matchup.overlap: Atlanta's run game (Bijan 34/167, 4.91 YPC; Allgeier 26/100) overlaps Carolina's soft front and the two missing defenders. Pitts (13 tgt, 96 yds, 66 air, about 5.1 aDOT) overlaps the 11.83 middle YPA more cleanly than London (19 tgt, 132 air). Carolina's overlap is split: McMillan (186 air, 168 yards) overlaps the Terrell absence, while Sanders, Renfrow and Hubbard's catches overlap the middle bleed and the blitz checkdown if Young is hurried.

form: Only weeks 1-2, so no season averages and no similar-defense sample. Bijan rush 24 and 143 (mean 83.5, exactly the stand-in), rec 100 and 25, rush+rec 124 and 168; the 143 and the 100-yard receiving game on -2 air yards look fluky, and the 24-yard rush is a real floor. Allgeier rush 24 and 76 vs 50.5. London 55 and 49 vs 52.5, glued to the number. Pitts 59 and 37 vs 48.5 (mean 48.0). McCloud 51 and 0. McMillan 68 and 100 vs 84.5 (mean 84.0), the only CAR receiver turning air into yards. Renfrow 11 and 48 on 130 air (3.9 yds/target). Legette 10 and -2 on 15 targets. Sanders 27 and 54 vs 40.5. Hubbard rush 57 and 38 (mean 47.5), rec 32 and 39, rush+rec 89 and 77. Dowdle rush 12 and 9. No OC/QB change is in the pack.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both leans lost. Carolina's 5.61 YPC was two-game noise, the Wharton backup held the point of attack, and the Allgeier committee (26 carries to Bijan's 34) plus a competitive home game left Bijan near 24 instead of 143. McMillan lost because Atlanta blitzed, Young checked down at a -0.35 EPA clip, and the yards went to Hubbard (already 71 receiving yards) and Sanders while an unnamed corner did not get beaten; Atlanta had allowed only four 20-plus throws for 60 yards and the real bleed was the middle, which is Pitts and Renfrow territory, not a 186-air outside profile. Both numbers were just two-game medians, so there was no priced edge if the matchup bump never showed, and unsaved outdoor weather could have cut the deep shots.
